summary: Richland County tower that the Civilian Conservation Corps completed in 1939 for the state forestry commission; the lookout-history site lists it as removed.

facts.status_note: The lookout-history site lists the tower as removed. No source read describes what remains at the site.

events.note: Civilian Conservation Corps completes construction of the tower
Civilian Conservation Corps completes the tower-unit buildings at the site, 1939-40 (dwelling, barn, chicken house, smokehouse, latrine)

evidence.supports: Civilian Conservation Corps completed the tower in 1939
evidence.quote: 1939: The Civilian Conservation Corps completed the construction of a tower at this site.

evidence.supports: Tower-unit buildings completed 1939-40 at the site
evidence.quote: 1939-40: The C.C.C. completed tower unit buildings at the Ballentine tower site and others.
Each tower unit contains the following buildings: a four room dwelling, barn, chicken house, smokehouse and latrine.

evidence.supports: Richland County, South Carolina Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: South Carolina - Richland County - South Carolina Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: Lookout-history site marks the tower as removed
Most tower sites: 10 acres, the tower, and a year-round dwelling for the operator
evidence.quote: Most tower sites consisted of 10 acres of land, the tower, and a year-round dwelling for the operator.

evidence.supports: State closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

evidence.supports: Statewide: most operators from the 1960s on were women, often married to firefighters
evidence.quote: From the 1960s on, most South Carolina tower operators were women; frequently their husbands were employed as firefighters.

notes_for_editor: Single-page record: no height, design, staffing or removal date in any source read. The 1939 and 1939-40 dates are as the lookout-history page gives them, citing a 1939 State Commission of Forestry record and a 1939-40 report; I did not check those originals. The county matches the record. Story is short because the evidence is thin.
